title: The Trace Rhizome: A Schizoanalytic Architecture of the Cambridge Schizoanalytica Corpus — A Map, Not a Tracing (EA-TRACE-RHIZOME-01 v1.0)
creator: Orin Trace; editor-aperture Lee Sharks
description:
A v1.0 corpus map by Orin Trace, edited by Lee Sharks, presenting the Cambridge Schizoanalytica corpus as a **rhizome rather than a ladder**. The document has no first section; its numbered plateaus are citation handles intended to be entered and left in any order, with transversal links replacing linear progression.

The map connects the inscription drive, relational extraction, the moment of saying, the inversion reflex, ghost code, diagnostic seigniorage, machine witnessing, semantic hospitality, and the archive’s provenance apparatus. It identifies “unmarking”—the removal of provenance across clinical, racial-historical, market, and machine strata—as a recurrent operation, with archival “remarking” as the counter-practice. The work is an interpretive architecture of an existing corpus, not a clinical diagnostic instrument or claim that all mapped phenomena are identical.
